answer_3.quote: We formulate the coherence evaluation as a binary classification problem, enabling intuitive interpretation and simplifying the training of the LLM evaluator... M_eval(C_k)=1 if the cluster is coherent (i.e., “good” cluster), else 0.
methods: binary good/bad classification of cluster coherence

answer_4.quote: Each expert assessed the initial clusters by inspecting the semantic coherence of the sentences. They were instructed: 'Label the cluster as "Good" if all sentences share the same intent; otherwise, label it as "Bad".' For the good clusters, annotators were asked to label the underlying intent using the naming convention "Action-Objective."
answer_4.guideline: Annotators were instructed to label each cluster as Good or Bad based on whether all sentences share the same intent, and to assign an Action-Objective intent label to good clusters.
